report:
Your results are about what your rating predicts: you scored 51% against 49% expected [F1], and you blundered about as often as similar-rated players would in the same positions (0.98 times expected) [F2].

## Biggest weaknesses

The data doesn't show any clear weakness. No opening family stands out once opponent rating and sample size are taken into account [F9]. Your blunder rates in every phase are close to your opponents' [F10][F11][F12]. One thing is worth keeping an eye on:

1. **Scotch Game as Black (worth watching, not confirmed).** You scored 21% here against 46% expected, but that's from only 12 games, and among 34 openings checked, one result this extreme is expected by luck alone [F8]. In moves 13-25 of these games you lost 6.2 win% per move, against 5.1 across all your games [F15]. Your worst games came through different lines: 4.c3 d5 5.Bb5 dxe4, the main line with 4.Nxd4 d6, and the Scotch Gambit 4.Bc4 [T1]. In that last game, 43...Kh7 lost 93 win% where Qxf4+ was available (https://www.chess.com/game/live/186801649660) [F16][T1].
   *What to do:* Choose one solid reply to 3.d4 and learn its typical middlegame plans, since that's where these games went wrong [F15].

## What's working

- **Low clock.** With under 10% of your time left, you made 75 blunders against 84.2 expected [F3]. Between 10% and 30% left, it was 61 against 73.0 [F4]. Neither result is clearly different from expected, but there's no sign that you collapse when short on time.
- **Queen's Gambit as White.** You scored 60% against 50% expected over 48 games, which counts as a possible strength [F6]. The median engine eval after move 12 was +1.0 for you [F13]. The Four Knights as Black also looks promising: 72% from 9 games [F7].

## Training plan

- Go over the three worst Scotch games [T1] and compare your moves to the engine's around moves 13-25, where you lose the most [F15].
- Middlegame is where you blunder most often, on 6.6% of moves [F11], so do middlegame puzzles regularly: https://lichess.org/training/middlegame [F19].
- Before each move, check for loose pieces, and drill hanging-piece puzzles: https://lichess.org/training/hangingPiece [F20]. Two examples of what to look for: 7...h5 missed Nxg4 (https://www.chess.com/game/live/186801191354) [F17], and 38...Qh2+ was played where Bf6 was better (https://www.chess.com/game/live/186706648876) [F18].
- Keep playing the Queen's Gambit as White and build on the advantages you get out of the opening [F13].
